title: Possessive Iḍāfa Construction
lede: Link nouns without an English apostrophe, let the final possessor control definiteness, and keep every case relationship visible.

items.feedback: The first noun is bare and the second definite and genitive.

items.prompt: What is always true of the second noun in an iḍāfa?
items.feedback: The muḍāf ilayh is always genitive; it may be definite or indefinite.

items.prompt: Can the first noun take tanwīn?
options: Only when the second noun is definite
items.feedback: The muḍāf does not take tanwīn.
An indefinite final possessor makes the whole iḍāfa indefinite.
A proper name can be the definite genitive possessor; the first noun remains bare.

items.prompt: Which noun controls the definiteness of the whole chain?
items.feedback: The end of the iḍāfa chain determines whether the whole construction is definite.
The indefinite possessor طَالِبٍ makes the whole phrase indefinite.
The final definite possessor makes the full phrase definite.
The suffix on the final possessor makes the chain definite.

options: The first noun is in construct state, not automatically indefinite in meaning
The first noun is always semantically indefinite
items.feedback: The muḍāf is morphologically bare, while definiteness comes from the final possessor.

items.prompt: Choose the subject form “The school door is open.”
items.feedback: The first noun is the nominative topic; the second remains genitive.
The first noun is accusative as the object; the possessor is still genitive.

items.prompt: Choose “I stood by the school door.”
items.feedback: After عِنْدَ, the first noun is genitive; the second is also genitive as possessor.

items.prompt: What controls the case of the first noun?
options: Its role in the wider sentence
The second noun always makes it genitive
items.feedback: The first noun can be nominative, accusative or genitive according to sentence role.

items.prompt: Choose “the school’s two students” as a nominative phrase.
items.feedback: Nominative dual muḍāf drops nūn: طَالِبَا.

items.prompt: Choose “I met the school’s two students.”
items.feedback: Accusative dual construct drops nūn; the following definite article produces طَالِبَيِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ in fully connected marking.

items.prompt: Choose “the school’s teachers” as a nominative phrase.
items.feedback: Nominative sound masculine plural muḍāf drops nūn: مُعَلِّمُو.

items.prompt: Choose “I spoke with the school’s teachers.”
items.feedback: Genitive sound masculine plural construct drops nūn: مُعَلِّمِي.
The masculine nominative adjective describes بَابُ.

items.prompt: Choose “the door of the large school”.
items.feedback: The feminine genitive adjective describes الْمَدْرَسَةِ.
An indefinite nominative adjective after a definite iḍāfa functions as the predicate.

The muḍāf is bare; the definite possessor is genitive.
The indefinite possessor makes the chain indefinite.
The proper name is the genitive possessor; مَرْيَمَ is diptote and shows fatḥa in the genitive.
The final suffix makes the full chain definite.
The first noun is accusative as the object; the final possessor is genitive.

items.prompt: Choose “the two classroom doors” as a nominative phrase.
items.feedback: Nominative dual muḍāf drops nūn.

items.prompt: Choose “the workers of the company” as a nominative phrase.
items.feedback: Nominative sound masculine plural construct drops nūn.

items.prompt: Which phrase means “the new student’s book”?
items.feedback: The genitive adjective describes the student.

items.prompt: Which phrase means “the student’s new book”?
items.feedback: The nominative masculine adjective describes كِتَابُ.

blocks: ## Iḍāfa builds precise noun relationships
Arabic links nouns directly to express ownership, type, part–whole relationships, institutions and many fixed names.
[ar] بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ
[ar] مُدِيرُ الشَّرِكَةِ
[ar] غُرْفَةُ النَّوْمِ
[ar] مَكْتَبَةُ مَدْرَسَتِنَا
[callout] Cambridge relevance: Iḍāfa appears constantly in signs, places, family relationships, school language, travel, work and extended descriptions.
## Choose your route
Secure the two-noun architecture before building chains and adjective scope.
### Core
- Build a two-noun iḍāfa.
- Remove الـ and tanwīn from the first noun.
- Place the second noun in the genitive.
### Develop
- Control definite and indefinite iḍāfa.
- Change the first noun’s case with sentence role.
- Build three-noun chains.
### Stretch
- Use dual and sound masculine plural construct forms.
- Resolve adjective scope accurately.
- Edit complex chains with names and suffixes.
## Readiness check
Retrieve the bare first noun, genitive possessor and definiteness rule.
## The two-part architecture
The first noun is the possessed or related item; the second noun identifies the possessor or relationship.

TABLE: Part | Arabic term | Core rule | Example // First noun | الْمُضَافُ | no الـ; no tanwīn; case comes from sentence role | بَابُ // Second noun | الْمُضَافُ إِلَيْهِ | always genitive; may be definite or indefinite | الْمَدْرَسَةِ

[callout/warning] Precision correction: the first noun is not automatically “indefinite”. It is in the construct state : morphologically bare, while the whole phrase may be definite or indefinite according to the final possessor.
[ar] بَابُ مَدْرَسَةٍ
[ar] بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ
[ar] بَابُ مَدْرَسَتِنَا
[ar] بَابُ مَدْرَسَةِ لَيْلَى
## The first noun changes case; the possessor stays genitive
Treat the iḍāfa as one unit inside the wider sentence.

TABLE: Sentence role | Model | Case pattern // Topic/subject | بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ مَفْتُوحٌ. | first nominative + second genitive // Direct object | فَتَحْتُ بَابَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ. | first accusative + second genitive // After a preposition/locator | وَقَفْتُ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ. | first genitive + second genitive
The genitive of the second noun belongs to the iḍāfa relationship. The case of the first noun belongs to the sentence around it.
## Longer iḍāfa chains
Every term except the final possessor remains bare; the final term controls definiteness.
[ar] بَابُ فَصْلِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ
[ar] مُدِيرُ مَكْتَبِ الشَّرِكَةِ
[ar] مَفَاتِيحُ سَيَّارَةِ أَبِي
[ar] بَرْنَامَجُ تَدْرِيبِ الْمُعَلِّمِينَ
[callout] Build from the end: decide the final possessor first, place it in the genitive, then add each preceding construct noun without الـ or tanwīn.
## Dual and sound masculine plural in iḍāfa
The same nūn-deletion rule used with attached possessive suffixes applies before a noun possessor.

TABLE: Independent form | Construct form | Example // طَالِبَانِ | طَالِبَا | طَالِبَا الْمَدْرَسَةِ // طَالِبَيْنِ | طَالِبَيِ | قَابَلْتُ طَالِبَيِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ // مُعَلِّمُونَ | مُعَلِّمُو | مُعَلِّمُو الْمَدْرَسَةِ // مُعَلِّمِينَ | مُعَلِّمِي | تَحَدَّثْتُ مَعَ مُعَلِّمِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ
Sound feminine plurals do not have a final nūn to delete: طَالِبَاتُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ remains structurally intact.
## Adjective scope: which noun is described?
The adjective normally follows the complete iḍāfa, so agreement evidence must identify its target.

TABLE: Meaning | Arabic | Agreement evidence // the school’s large door | بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ الْكَبِيرُ | masculine nominative adjective describes بَابُ // the door of the large school | بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ الْكَبِيرَةِ | feminine genitive adjective describes الْمَدْرَسَةِ // the school door is large | بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ كَبِيرٌ | indefinite nominative predicate
[callout/warning] Nearest noun is not enough. Use gender, number, definiteness and case together. The adjective’s form tells you which noun it can describe.
## Names, suffixes and established expressions
The final possessor can take several forms.

TABLE: Final possessor type | Example | Meaning // Definite common noun | كِتَابُ الطَّالِبِ | the student’s book // Indefinite common noun | كِتَابُ طَالِبٍ | a student’s book // Proper name | كِتَابُ لَيْلَى | Layla’s book // Possessive suffix | كِتَابُ صَدِيقِي | my friend’s book // Longer chain | كِتَابُ صَدِيقِ أَخِي | my brother’s friend’s book

[callout] Case-aware name note: some proper names are diptotes and show fatḥa in the genitive, such as مَدْرَسَةُ مَرْيَمَ . This is Stretch recognition; the core skill is recognising the proper name as the final possessor.
## Proofreading clinic
Check the first noun, final possessor, chain definiteness and adjective target.

TABLE: Draft | Improved version | Reason // الْبَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ | بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ | The first noun cannot take الـ. // بَابٌ الْمَدْرَسَةِ | بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ | The first noun cannot take tanwīn. // بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةُ | بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ | The possessor is genitive. // بَابُ مَدْرَسَةٍ الْكَبِيرُ | بَابُ مَدْرَسَةٍ كَبِيرٌ / بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ الْكَبِيرُ | Definiteness and intended meaning must be made clear. // طَالِبَانِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ | طَالِبَا الْمَدْرَسَةِ | Dual construct drops nūn. // مُعَلِّمُونَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ | مُعَلِّمُو الْمَدْرَسَةِ | Sound masculine plural construct drops nūn. // بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ الْكَبِيرَةُ | بَابُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ الْكَبِيرَةِ | An adjective describing the genitive school is also genitive.
## Game: Build the noun chain
Choose the iḍāfa that carries the intended meaning and case.
## Skills workshop
Decode and produce iḍāfa in descriptions, signs and connected writing.
### Reading: unpack the chains
زُرْنَا مَعْرِضَ فُنُونِ الْمَدِينَةِ، ثُمَّ دَخَلْنَا قَاعَةَ أَعْمَالِ الطُّلَّابِ. أَعْجَبَتْنِي لَوْحَةُ طَالِبِ مَدْرَسَتِنَا الْمَوْهُوبِ.
Bracket each iḍāfa chain. Explain why الْمَوْهُوبِ describes the male student rather than the feminine school, using agreement evidence.
### Speaking: describe a place
Give a 60-second tour of a school, house, town or workplace using eight iḍāfa expressions, including one chain of three nouns.
### A place and its relationships
Write 110–130 Arabic words describing a school, home, workplace, town or fictional venue.
[callout] Success checklist: Use at least ten iḍāfa constructions: two indefinite, four definite, two with proper names or suffixes, one dual/SMP construct and one adjective-scope contrast.
[callout] Paper route: Draw a chain diagram for each long iḍāfa. Mark the first noun’s sentence case and underline every genitive possessor.
## Final mastery check
Show that you can control architecture, definiteness, case, number and adjective scope.
### You can now
- Build definite and indefinite iḍāfa accurately.
- Explain why the first noun is bare rather than automatically indefinite.
- Change the first noun’s case while keeping the possessor genitive.
- Build longer chains.
- Delete dual and sound masculine plural nūn.
- Resolve adjective scope through agreement.
Spaced revisit: collect ten iḍāfa expressions from previous lessons and classify their final possessor.
